complaint_text: A direct debit from EDP in the amount of €84.50 appeared on my account, which I never authorized, as I had already canceled that service last month. I want an immediate refund of the returned amount.

I requested the cancellation of the bank guarantee I provided for my tenant over two months ago, given that the lease agreement has ended and he returned the keys. They continue to charge me the quarterly guarantee fee and have not cancelled the guarantee.

I requested the addition of my wife as a second joint holder on my current account three weeks ago. We submitted all documentation at the branch, but so far they have not updated the customer file and she cannot access the account via the app.

I opened a 12-month fixed-term deposit of 10,000 euros. The term ended last week and the money was transferred to my current account, but I was not credited with the interest due according to the agreed rate of 2.5% TANB.

I tried to top up my prepaid card with 50 euros using the mobile app. The amount was debited from my main current account, but the balance on the electronic money card remains zero and I am unable to make purchases.

I deposited a cheque from another bank at the branch last Tuesday. They told me it would be available in 48 hours, but 5 business days have passed and the cheque remains uncleared without any valid explanation.

I received a notification that my account was frozen due to a tax authority garnishment order. However, they withheld my entire balance, violating the national minimum wage limit which is exempt from attachment by law.

I called customer support four times this week to resolve a simple issue and I am always kept on hold for over 30 minutes until the call drops. It is an absolute lack of respect and abysmal service delivery.
I was charged a credit maintenance fee of 15 euros on my mortgage loan that was not specified in the ESIS (FIN) or in the initial home loan contract.

My company holds an ICO COVID-19 guaranteed loan and we requested an early repayment of €20,000. The bank is creating bureaucratic obstacles and demanding unnecessary documents just to delay the process.
The interest rate applied to this month's installment of my personal loan increased without any prior notice or explanation, exceeding the benchmark index agreed upon in the contract.
I went to the branch counter to withdraw 400 euros in cash, and the staff member handed me two clearly torn 50€ banknotes taped together, refusing to exchange them on the spot.
My debit card expired, and I requested its definitive cancellation a month ago as I no longer needed it. However, they issued a new card and charged me the annual fee of 25 euros.
I use my revolving credit card and noticed that this month they charged installment processing fees and administrative expenses again, which I consider abusive and unitemized.

I made an international wire transfer to an account in the United States (outside the SEPA zone). The money left my account 10 days ago, has not reached the recipient yet, and I was already charged €45 in operational fees.
I checked my risk statement at the Central Credit Register (CIRBE) and noticed my name is still tied to an outstanding loan balance that I fully settled last year. I demand an immediate correction.
I received a SEPA direct debit from Vodafone on my account, but the amount charged is €120 when my monthly invoice is only €35. I want to reject the charge and get a refund for the difference.
My company issued a bank guarantee and the beneficiary requested its enforcement. However, the bank executed the guarantee without verifying that the contractual requirements for calling it were met.
I have been trying to open a savings account via home banking for a week, but the system keeps throwing a contract validation error at the final step, preventing the formalization of the contract.
I prematurely closed my €5,000 term deposit. I knew I would forfeit the interest, but the bank also deducted €100 from my invested principal as a penalty, which is unlawful.
The balance on my virtual prepaid card expired, and the institution refuses to refund the remaining €35.40 I had stored there, claiming the funds have lapsed.
I paid for a purchase with a cheque issued by your institution, but the merchant states the cheque was returned for alleged lack of funds, even though I had more than enough balance in my account.
I was subject to a court garnishment on my bank account, and the bank froze my entire balance without notifying me or specifying the court case reference number.

I submitted a formal complaint to the Customer Service Department (SAC) over two months ago regarding an improper fee. They replied stating they would refund the amount, but to date they have failed to implement the decision.
I am trying to renegotiate the terms of my mortgage loan to restructure the debt due to financial hardship, but the bank refuses to evaluate my request for refinancing/dation in payment.
I requested the consolidation and refinancing of the personal loans my company holds with your bank, but you are taking months to respond to the viability plan presented.
I requested a refinancing of my consumer loan installments due to temporary unemployment, but the bank rejected the restructuring agreement without offering any justification.
I went to buy foreign currency (USD) at the branch for a trip, and they applied an exchange rate completely out of line with market rates, along with a hidden fee.
The bank unilaterally blocked my credit card without sending an SMS or email warning, leaving me unable to pay for my hotel while traveling abroad.
Last month I received my revolving card statement and noticed the applied interest rate went from 18% to 22% without any contractual modification being communicated to me.
I sent an international transfer to the UK on the 2nd, and by the 12th the beneficiary had still not received the funds, even though the amount was debited from my account on the very same day.
It shows on my CIRBE statement at the Bank of Spain that I have a defaulted amount with your bank, but I have a final court ruling declaring that debt completely null and void.
I have an unauthorized debit of €49.99 on my current account from a company called 'TechServices' that I have never heard of and never gave direct debit authorization to.
I provided a bank guarantee for a public tender. The tender ended and the public entity issued the guarantee release document, yet the bank refuses to proceed with its cancellation.
I submitted all required documentation to change account holders on my current account following my father's passing, but the process has been stalled for 3 months without updates.
I hold a term deposit, and upon maturity, the bank calculated the net interest by applying an incorrect withholding tax and failing to honor the rate agreed upon.
I loaded €100 onto my digital wallet/prepaid card via ATM. The balance did not reflect in the system, and when I requested a refund from customer support, they said they couldn't do anything.
I ordered a chequebook from the bank, they charged me the issuance fee, but the cheques never arrived at my address and were lost without the bank offering a resolution.
I received a tax authority garnishment order on my account and the bank charged a garnishment processing fee of €50, which I find abusive and disproportionate.
I submitted a formal written complaint at my local branch last month regarding poor service from a staff member, and to this day I haven't received a response or case number.
I requested a change in the security of my mortgage loan (property collateral substitution), but the risk department is imposing absurd requirements and stalling the decision for months.
My micro-enterprise requested a restructuring of an unsecured working capital loan during the crisis, but the bank refused to execute the approved refinancing plan.
I have a personal loan and paid the installment on time this month, but the bank charged me late payment interest claiming the payment posted after the daily cutoff time.

I went to the teller to withdraw €1,500 in cash, and the staff member gave me €100 less than the amount signed on the receipt. When I complained immediately, they claimed the till balanced and refused to recount.
I canceled my credit card via registered letter within the legal timeframe, but the bank continued sending me statements charging the following year's annual fee.
I have a revolving card and have been paying monthly installments dutifully for years, but the outstanding principal barely decreases due to 24% interest rates and fees never explained to me.
I made an international transfer in USD to a supplier in Mexico, and undisclosed intermediary bank charges were deducted, causing the amount to arrive incomplete.
I am trying to get a new loan at another bank and was rejected because your bank reported overdue balances to CIRBE, whereas my account is 100% settled without any arrears.
A direct debit was processed on my bank account by an insurance company, even though the insurance policy had been canceled by mutual agreement three months ago.
The bank executed the bank guarantee issued for my company without prior notification of the payment demand made by the creditor.
I demand a copy of the original current account agreement signed in 2015, but the bank is charging me €30 to issue copies of contractual documentation.
I subscribed to a term deposit with quarterly interest settlement, but last quarter the amount deposited into my account was lower than the net value contractually agreed.
I tried to redeem the funds remaining on my prepaid card and the bank informed me they charge a 10% redemption fee, violating electronic money regulations.
I sent a cheque drawn on my account to pay for a service, and the bank dishonored the payment claiming non-existent alterations on the document.
I received a legal garnishment notice and the bank froze not only my individual account, but also the joint account I hold with my mother, impacting her funds.
The Customer Ombudsman ruled in my favor regarding improper fee charges, but my local branch refuses to credit the money back into my account.
The bank is charging me monthly mortgage processing fees that were not included in the terms agreed upon when signing the deed.
I requested an extension and refinancing of the personal guarantee loan my business holds for working capital, but the bank's proposal demands disproportionate additional collateral.
My consumer loan has a fixed interest rate, but this month I noticed the charged installment was higher than last month's without any change in rate or term.
During in-person service at the teller counter to deposit store cash earnings, the employee miscounted the bills and recorded €50 less on the receipt than the actual amount.
I discovered three online debit card transactions totaling €320 on a foreign website that I never made nor authorized via SMS verification code.
I hold a credit card in revolving mode, and upon requesting full settlement of the balance, the bank presented an unfounded residual amount with unitemized fees.
I made an international wire transfer outside Europe and was charged issuance fees twice on the same transaction due to a system glitch.
In the Bank of Spain CIRBE record, your bank reported that I am a guarantor for a €50,000 debt, but I never signed any guarantor agreement.
I have my electricity bill on direct debit and the bank bounced the payment alleging insufficient funds, when in fact I had plenty of balance in the account.
The bank refuses to issue a certificate of guarantee discharge/cancellation, even though the primary obligation was fully performed months ago.
I changed my account signature rules to require joint signatures, but the bank allowed a transfer authorized by only one of the joint holders.
The yield generated and credited upon maturity of my term deposit did not correspond to the interest rate agreed in the signed commercial offer.
My reloadable prepaid card was blocked due to alleged inactivity, and they charged me an inactive balance maintenance fee that wiped out my remaining funds.
I was charged a returned cheque fee for a cheque I deposited, with the bank claiming the issuer had insufficient funds, but the fee amount is abusive.

I've been trying to solve a mortgage problem for weeks. I went to the branch and was told to call support; I called support and was told it must be handled at the branch. Nobody takes responsibility and everyone passes the buck. Meanwhile, this month I was charged a €40 late payment fee because the direct debit failed due to a glitch in the bank's own system. I demand a refund of this fee caused by your failure and that customers be treated with basic professional respect.

Good afternoon. I am writing because I am deeply outraged by what happened last Friday. I went to your bank's ATM at the shopping center to deposit €300 in cash into my current account. The machine swallowed the bills, displayed an error on screen, gave no receipt, and did not credit the money to my account. To make matters worse, I asked for help at the branch and the staff member treated me poorly, saying I had to wait for the till reconciliation, and I still don't have my money, which prevented me from paying an electricity bill that has now expired.

I sent all paperwork to change account ownership following my father's passing in January. It has been 4 months! Every time I go there, they request another document they hadn't asked for before. Customer service is shameful. To top it off, they keep charging €8 account maintenance fees every month on an account that should be undergoing ownership transfer and closure. I want this resolved once and for all and a refund of fees wrongfully charged during this unwarranted delay.

On March 10th I initiated a bank transfer to the UK to pay for an urgent medical equipment order for my business. I chose the option with fees charged to me to ensure the recipient received the exact amount. After 15 days, the supplier said they hadn't received the money. I called the bank and it took them 4 days just to tell me the transfer was held for data validation. The delay caused the cancellation of the order and massive losses for my business, besides charging me a €50 transfer fee.

I would like to file a formal complaint regarding the management of my account. Last month I noticed €150 debited under the description of a tax authority garnishment. However, the tax debt had been settled the previous week and I presented proof at the branch. The account manager said he would cancel the hold in the system, but failed to do so in time and the money was withdrawn. Now I am out of money and the bank says it's the Tax Authority's fault. It was clear negligence by the manager.

I applied for a €5,000 personal loan through your website three weeks ago. The application was approved and I was told the funds would land in my account within 24 hours. Up to this day, I haven't seen a single cent. I send emails and nobody replies, I call support and they say it's processing. To top off the absurdity, I already received an email statement charging the first installment and interest for money I never received in my account! Resolve this urgently.

My revolving card has been a nightmare. In 2021 I requested a €2,000 credit limit and since then I have paid the fixed monthly installment of €60 every single month without fail. I checked the detailed statement this month and noticed the outstanding balance remains almost identical to the initial amount! I discovered you are applying an exorbitant interest rate and adding unrequested insurance and management fees. Statement wording is completely opaque and deliberately confusing so customers don't realize how much interest they pay.

I hereby complain about the reporting of my personal data to CIRBE at the Bank of Spain. I applied for an auto loan and the finance company rejected it because they said I had an overdue debt of €1,200 registered with your bank. The problem is that this debt relates to a credit card stolen from me in 2023, an incident reported to the police and submitted to the bank with the police report at the time. You canceled the card back then but left the fraudulent debt under my name and reported delinquency to the authorities.

Dear Sirs, I am expressing my deep dissatisfaction. I requested a payment account transfer from your bank to another financial institution under the switching scheme. The destination bank handled everything, but you failed to transfer standing orders and direct debits within the legal timeframe. Result: my home water bill was not paid via direct debit and my service was disconnected. Beyond this huge inconvenience, you are still charging me account closure fees.

I have held a mortgage loan with your bank for 8 years. Recently I requested a novation of terms to switch from variable rate to fixed rate, matching current market offers. I submitted all required documentation in early January. 3 months have passed, the bank keeps stalling, asking for the same documents repeatedly, and in the meantime Euribor rose again, making my monthly payment jump by 80 euros this month due to pure inertia and delay from the bank's underwriting department.

hi so look, 45 euros were taken from my account for a vodafone direct debit that i already canceled in the app last month. don't get why you paid it if it was canceled. called to complain and the agent was super rude and hung up on my face without refunding my money. demand my money put back in my account asap pls.

went to withdraw a 20 bill at bank x atm on main st today and machine gave me a torn bill taped in the middle. went straight to teller to exchange the bill and guy said he couldn't do anything cause money came out of machine and not his problem. how does a bank put damaged notes in atms and refuse to swap for customer? want my 20€ in a proper bill.

writing because on this month debit card statement there are two purchases of 89€ each made at an online store 'Zalando' that i never made in my life. wasnt even home at that time and card was always with me in my wallet. called bank to cancel card for fraud and lady who answered said it was probably my fault for putting details where i shouldn't and now have to wait 30 days for them to check refund. ridiculous service.

applied for a personal loan to buy a used car last month. everything fine at start but now saw interest table and charging much higher rate than the TANB rate told at desk when signing papers. feel cheated wanted the right rate promised at counter not this ripped off value.

did a transfer to an account in Spain and charged 12 euros fee. problem isn't just fee which is expensive, but money took 1 week to get there and person i sent money to had late interest to pay cause of your delay. bank said fault is intermediary bank outside sepa zone but my contract is with you.

I am facing a severe issue in my business due to a bank guarantee requested for a public contract. The work was delivered and accepted by the city council, which issued the certificate of liability termination. I presented that document at your branch over a month ago to cancel the guarantee and stop charging me the fee. Not only do you continue debiting the €120 fee from my account, but customer support says you lost the original document I delivered at the counter.

My bank account is subject to repeated wrongful charges. They charge a €5 maintenance fee plus stamp duty on an account used exclusively to pay my mortgage installment and holding no other linked services. I have filed two complaints in the complaint book at the branch and to date not a single cent of improperly charged fees over the last year has been refunded.

I want to register my dissatisfaction with your institution's lack of professionalism. I went to the bank to renew my term deposit, and the employee persuaded me to place the money into a different financial product claiming it had guaranteed yield just like a term deposit. Now I checked and it was actually a risky product where I lost part of my capital. When I complained, they said I signed contractual documentation and should have read all fine print. This is misleading advertising and lack of transparency.

I have an old debt from a revolving credit card that was fully paid off over two years ago. I hold the debt discharge statement issued by the bank itself. Imagine my surprise when applying for business financing this week, I discovered my name remains listed on Bank of Spain's CIRBE as a debtor for that same amount. You are severely damaging my business activity and I demand immediate removal of this false record.

My reloadable prepaid card stopped working out of nowhere when trying to pay for lunch at a restaurant. I had around 80 euros in balance. I tried reloading via home banking to see if it reactivated; money left my current account but didn't enter the card. I called support and they said the card had expired and to recover my money I had to pay a €15 admin fee. It's theft keeping money that belongs to me.

I purchased a €1,200 vacation trip with my credit card. The travel agency went bankrupt and closed without providing the service. I submitted a chargeback / transaction dispute request to the bank providing proof of the company's cancellation. The bank refuses to process the refund on my account and keeps demanding payment of credit card installments on monthly statements as if nothing happened.

I was targeted by an SMS scam and made a bank transfer under deception. About 10 minutes later, realizing the mistake, I immediately called the bank to request transfer cancellation or a hold on the target account funds. The agent took forever to answer and said they couldn't do anything because the transfer was already processed. Customer support was completely ineffective in providing immediate assistance to mitigate fraud.

I received an email from the bank saying terms for my current account would change and account maintenance fee would rise from €2 to €7 per month starting next month. They failed to give the legal 60-day advance notice required to allow account cancellation if I disagreed. Furthermore, the account closure process on the website constantly errors out, forcing customers to go in person to the branch and waste hours in line.

I am furious about my mortgage loan situation. I made an early partial prepayment of 10,000 euros to reduce outstanding debt. The bank processed the prepayment but applied a prepayment fee higher than the maximum limit legally allowed for variable-rate loans. I tried complaining at the branch, but my account manager was extremely rude and refused to recalculate.

My SME initiated a financial restructuring and refinancing process for a personal guarantee loan. The bank took four months to approve the proposed payment plan, and in the meantime flagged the company as delinquent, applying penalty interest during the period the file was stalled awaiting validation from the bank's own risk department. This is unacceptable behavior suffocating businesses.

I had an issue at an ATM where I tried to withdraw 100 euros. The machine spent a long time processing, didn't dispense cash, and returned my card. Right after, I received a notification on my phone stating a €100 debit was made on my current account. I filed a claim on the same day and 3 weeks have passed without the debited money being credited back to my account.

The bank blocked my access to home banking without any prior notice. When I called customer support, they said it was for customer data updating and ID document validation. The issue is that I had already submitted my updated ID card last month through the platform itself. Due to this improper block, I couldn't process my employees' payroll payments on the due date.

I requested a change in signature rules and removal of a former partner from the company's bank account. We submitted the updated corporate certificate showing the partner's resignation. The bank still demands the physical presence and signature of the removed partner to update account records, which is impossible since he no longer holds any connection to the company. Lack of update is preventing the business from operating the account.

I am writing to formalize a complaint regarding my revolving credit card. I requested a change in the monthly installment amount to pay off debt faster, but the bank ignored my request and maintained minimum installment charges, drastically increasing total interest burdens over time. I feel I am being pushed into perpetual debt without transparency.

I requested the cancellation of my debit card in January after it was stolen. They charged me a €15 card replacement fee, which I accepted. However, next month my account statement showed the annual fee charged again for the old card that was already canceled and destroyed in the system. Beyond the duplicate improper charge, customer support forces me to pay for premium hotline calls whenever I try calling to fix errors made by the bank itself.
